chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ‘Umar ibn Sa‘d [‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Hāni’ ibn Hāni’, from ‘Alī (peace be upon him)
He said: ‘Verily al-Ḥusayn will be killed a killing, and indeed I know the dust of the land on which he will be killed, which is close to the two rivers.’
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the location of Imam Husain's martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from Kamil al-Ziyarat underscores the precise geographical foreknowledge of Imam ‘Alī (a.s.) regarding Karbala, identifying the specific terrain near the 'two rivers' (likely the Euphrates and its tributaries) where al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) would be martyred. It serves as a key evidence for the infallible knowledge (‘ilm) of the Ahl al-Bayt and connects the event to the broader prophetic tradition of predicting future trials. The mention of the specific location adds a layer of historical realism to the eschatological significance of the martyrdom.
